steps.title: French is not read like English
steps.body:
French uses the same letters as English, but they often make different sounds.

The good news: French spelling follows rules, and the rules are very regular. In this course you learn them one at a time.

You will start by hearing French, not only reading it.

steps.title: Most last letters are silent
steps.body:
In French, the last letter of a word is very often not said. You see the letter, but you do not pronounce it.

Listen to these words and notice what you do not hear.

There are exceptions. The letters c, r, f and l are often said at the end, as in avec, bonjour, neuf and sel. You will practise them later.

steps.prompt: Which letter is silent at the end of this word?
steps.explain: The last letter, t, is silent. You say puh-TEE.

steps.title: Every syllable counts
steps.body:
English puts a strong stress on one syllable, like PHO-to-graph. French is different: each syllable has almost the same length and force.

Think of a steady beat: ta, ta, ta. The only small lift is on the last syllable of a group of words.

examples.en: ka-na-DA, an even beat with a small lift at the end

steps.title: You already read French every day
steps.body:
If you live in Canada, you see French on road signs, packages and shop doors.

Now you will hear how these words really sound. Notice the silent last letters in arrêt and ouvert.

steps.explain: Sortie means exit. You will see it above doors in Canada.

steps.question: What does the sign say?
steps.explain: Arrêt means stop. The final t is silent, so you say a-RAY.

steps.prompt: Complete the rule: in French, the last letter of a word is…
steps.explain: Often silent. So listen first, then read.

steps.tip: Say it slowly: bon-JOUR. Keep both syllables the same length.

steps.title: What comes next
steps.body:
Next you learn the alphabet and how to spell your name out loud. Then you learn the sounds one group at a time.

You do not need to memorise anything today. Just listen a lot, and use Ask Marie whenever a sound feels strange.
